candidates.summary: Tennessee officials were unable to execute Christa Gail Pike after administering two doses of a lethal-injection drug. She was taken to a medical facility, and Gov. Bill Lee halted the state’s remaining executions for the rest of 2026.
candidates.title: Tennessee execution attempt fails; governor halts remaining 2026 executions

candidates.summary: A copilot stabbed the pilot of a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv and apparently tried to crash the aircraft, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said. Passengers and crew subdued the attacker, and the plane carrying about 170 people landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
candidates.title: Passengers intervene after pilot is stabbed on Israel-bound flight
candidates.geography: Saudi Arabia; United Arab Emirates; Israel

candidates.summary: The U.S. military said it completed the withdrawal of all American troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission against the Islamic State group. The withdrawal was carried out under an agreement reached two years earlier with Iraq.
candidates.title: U.S. military completes troop withdrawal from Iraq

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials said a Russian missile-and-drone barrage killed seven people, including a child, and primarily targeted the country’s power grid. The overnight attack caused power outages as Ukraine prepared for colder weather.
candidates.title: Russian barrage kills seven and targets Ukraine’s power grid

candidates.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a new U.S. military drone command and directed the services to reduce positions for generals and admirals by 20%. Pentagon officials said the senior-rank reduction is to be completed by January 1, 2027.
candidates.title: Pentagon announces drone command and deeper senior-rank cuts

candidates.summary: The State Department removed Syria from a list of countries subject to a general policy of denying licenses and approvals for U.S. weapons and munitions exports. The regulatory change does not itself approve arms sales, which remain subject to licensing.
candidates.title: U.S. removes Syria from general arms-export denial policy

candidates.summary: Republican and Democratic senators announced an agreement on legislation intended to shorten federal reviews for energy and infrastructure projects. The proposal would also require regulators to address the costs that large electricity users, including AI data centers, impose on power systems. A vote was not expected until after the November midterm elections.
candidates.title: U.S. senators reach bipartisan permitting agreement

candidates.summary: Iranian state media said authorities executed two men convicted over violence during nationwide anti-government protests in January. Their death sentences had been upheld by Iran’s Supreme Court, according to the report.
candidates.title: Iran executes two men over alleged roles in January protest violence
